Exercise: Recumbent Bike

Category:
cardio

Exercise Type:
None

Force Type:
None

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- linear

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes
- hamstrings

Equipment:

- machine

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
3

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: Severe back pain, reason: The seated position may exacerbate symptoms in some individuals.
- condition: Recent knee surgery, reason: High resistance levels can put undue stress on the knees.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Interval Training, description: Alternate between high-resistance intervals and low-resistance recovery intervals to enhance cardiovascular fitness.
- name: Sprint Intervals, description: Perform short bursts of intense pedaling followed by rest periods to improve anaerobic capacity.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Stationary Bike, reason: similar cardiovascular benefits and lower impact

Instructions:

- To begin, seat yourself on the bike and adjust the seat to your height.
- Select the desired option from the menu. You may have to start pedaling to turn it on. You can use the manual setting, or you can select a program to use. Typically, you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise. The level of resistance can be changed throughout the workout. The handles can be used to monitor your heart rate to help you stay at an appropriate intensity.
- Recumbent bikes offer convenience, cardiovascular benefits, and have less impact than other activities. A 150 lb person will burn about 230 calories cycling at a moderate rate for 30 minutes, compared to 450 calories or more running.
